fullPassage:
Back on February 9, 1795, something remarkable happened in front of Changdeokgung Palace, where King Jeongjo lived. There was quite a crowd gathered there to witness a very special procession that's still talked about in Korea today.

More than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and lots of important officials, all marching alongside the king and his mother with 50 musicians playing traditional instruments. When they crossed a bridge made of 36 boats on the Hangang River, you can imagine how that turned heads!

Lasting four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession moved alongside the king and his mother as they made a round trip to Hwaseong Haenggung.

The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was to show respect to his family. It happened around his mother's sixtieth birthday. His father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung. He was planning to hold a memorial service to honor his late father.

King Jeongjo was also making a statement about the Joseon Dynasty's strength. He dressed up like a military leader, wearing armor and sitting on a horse with his soldiers marching in perfect order.

The procession also had something to do with Hwaseong Fortress, which was being built. He wanted it to be a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade as he hoped to make it the new capital, away from all the political chaos in Hanyang. So King Jeongjo gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them bring together the finest architectural techniques of his time from both the East and the West to build Hwaseong Fortress.

He treated his people well during the construction of the fortress. They received fair wages and breaks during bad weather and were even paid when they were sick, something that was unheard of at that time. Once people got wind of King Jeongjo's plan, workers from all over the country came together in a rush. So, in under three years was the project finished, though it was initially thought to take about 10 years.

The procession was actually a way for ordinary people to get up close and personal with the king. King Jeongjo set up a chance during the procession for common people to meet him and to share their concerns.

Through the procession, King Jeongjo made government more accessible. He added special exams during the procession, giving more people a shot at joining the government.

He made sure everything was documented properly by creating records for the procession and the construction of Hwaseong Fortress. These construction records were especially a lifesaver when the fortress was damaged during wartime. They were even part of why UNESCO recognized Hwaseong Fortress as a World Heritage Site.

Among the records of the procession, there are these amazing paintings. One painting, Hwaneo Haengryeoldo, doesn't just feature the king's crew, but it also shows ordinary people watching along the road.

King Jeongjo's 1795 procession and Hwaseong Fortress stand as proof of that spirit. Hwaseong is more than just a fortress; it symbolizes a king who cared for his people.

questions.passage: Back on February 9, 1795, something remarkable happened in front of Changdeokgung Palace, where King Jeongjo lived. There was quite a crowd gathered there to witness a very special procession that's still talked about in Korea today. More than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and lots of important officials, all marching alongside the king and his mother with 50 musicians playing traditional instruments.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 1795년 2월 9일, 창덕궁 앞에서 특별한 행렬이 있었다. 2,000명 이상의 군인, 수백 명의 기마병, 많은 관리들이 왕과 어머니와 함께 행진했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② The procession included more than 2,000 soldiers: 원문과 일치 ❌ ① The event took place at Gyeongbokgung Palace: 창덕궁이 맞음 ❌ ③ The procession was organized by the queen: 정조가 주관 ❌ ④ There were 100 musicians in the procession: 50명이 맞음
det.tip: 숫자 정보를 정확히 확인하세요: 2,000+ soldiers, 50 musicians, Changdeokgung Palace.

ch: The event took place at Gyeongbokgung Palace.
The procession included more than 2,000 soldiers.
The procession was organized by the queen.
There were 100 musicians in the procession.

questions.passage: The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was to show respect to his family. It happened around his mother's sixtieth birthday. And his father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung. He was planning to hold a memorial service to honor his late father. By combining the two events, he was telling everyone how much family meant to him.
questions.stem: 정조의 행차 목적으로 본문에 언급되지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 행차 목적: 어머니 60세 생신 + 아버지 추모 제사 + 가족 중시 메시지. '외국 사신 접대'는 언급되지 않았다.
det.analysis: ❌ ① To celebrate his mother's sixtieth birthday: 본문에 언급됨 ❌ ② To hold a memorial service for his late father: 본문에 언급됨 ❌ ③ To show how much family meant to him: 본문에 언급됨 ✅ ④ To welcome foreign ambassadors: 본문에 없음
det.tip: 불일치 문제 — 본문에 없는 내용을 찾으세요.

ch: To celebrate his mother's sixtieth birthday
To hold a memorial service for his late father
To show how much family meant to him

questions.passage: Lasting four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession moved alongside the king and his mother as they made a round trip to Hwaseong Haenggung. When they crossed a bridge made of 36 boats on the Hangang River, you can imagine how that turned heads!
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용으로 보아 다음 중 옳은 것은?

det.korean: 행렬은 4일간 68km를 이동했고, 한강에 36척의 배로 만든 다리를 건넜다.
det.analysis: ❌ ① The procession lasted six days: 4일 ❌ ② The total distance was 86 kilometers: 68km ✅ ③ A bridge of 36 boats was used to cross the Hangang River: 원문 일치 ❌ ④ The procession was a one-way trip: 왕복(round trip)
det.tip: 숫자를 정확히 대조하세요: 4 days, 68 km, 36 boats, round trip.

ch: A bridge of 36 boats was used to cross the Hangang River.
The procession was a one-way trip.

questions.passage: King Jeongjo was also making a statement about the Joseon Dynasty's strength. He dressed up like a military leader, (A) [wore / wearing] armor and sitting on a horse with his soldiers (B) [marching / marched] in perfect order. It was a way of (C) [saying / to say], "We're ready to protect our land."
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 갑옷을 (A)입고(wearing) 말 위에 앉아, 병사들이 완벽한 질서로 (B)행진하는(marching) 가운데. '~하는 방법'이라는 뜻의 a way of (C)saying.
det.analysis: ✅ ② (A) wearing — (B) marching — (C) saying: 분사구문+현재분사+전치사 of 뒤 동명사 ❌ ① wore는 분사구문이 아닌 과거 시제 ❌ ③ marched는 능동 의미의 현재분사가 적절 ❌ ④ to say는 전치사 of 뒤에 올 수 없음
det.tip: of + V-ing (동명사). 분사구문: wearing(입으면서), marching(행진하는).

questions.passage: He treated his people well during the construction of the fortress. They received fair wages and breaks during bad weather and were even paid when they were sick, something that was ①<u>unheard</u> of at that time. Back then, ordinary people were typically ②<u>required</u> to work on public projects without ③<u>getting</u> paid. Once people got wind of King Jeongjo's plan, workers from all over the country came together in a rush. So, in under three years ④<u>were</u> the project finished.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: 3년 이내에 프로젝트가 완성되었다. 주어 the project는 단수이므로 ④ were → was가 되어야 한다. 도치구문: 'in under three years was the project finished'.
det.analysis: ✅ ①②③ 어법 적절 ❌ ④ were → was: 주어 the project(단수) + 도치구문
det.tip: 도치구문에서도 주어-동사 수 일치는 유지됩니다. the project(단수) → was.

questions.passage: The procession wasn't just some fancy show for ordinary people. It was actually a way for them to get up close and personal with the king. King Jeongjo set up a chance during the procession for common people to meet him and to share their concerns. This was a big deal, especially for those who couldn't read or write. They didn't have any other way to tell the king what was on their minds, so this was __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 행렬은 백성이 왕에게 직접 자신의 고민을 전할 수 있는 유일한 기회였다. 읽고 쓸 수 없는 사람에게 특히 중요했으므로, '왕에게 직접 연결되는 통로'라는 의미.
det.analysis: ✅ ② a direct line to him: 원문 그대로 '왕에게 직접 연결되는 통로' ❌ ① a formal written petition: 읽고 쓸 수 없다고 했으므로 부적절 ❌ ③ an annual festival for entertainment: 오락이 아니라 소통의 기회 ❌ ④ a military training exercise: 군사 훈련과 무관
det.tip: a direct line to = ~에게 직접 연결되는 통로. 문맥에서 '유일한 소통 수단'을 파악하세요.

questions.passage:
He made sure everything was documented properly by creating records for the procession and the construction of Hwaseong Fortress. These construction records were especially a lifesaver when the fortress was damaged during wartime. They were even part of why UNESCO recognized Hwaseong Fortress as a World Heritage Site.

At first, the people at UNESCO were a bit unsure about recognizing Hwaseong Fortress as the real deal. They weren't totally convinced it was authentic. But after checking out translated documents and comparing them with the restored fortress, they finally came around and agreed that the fortress had actually been __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유네스코는 처음에 화성의 진정성을 의심했지만, 번역 문서와 복원된 요새를 비교한 후 요새가 원래 의도대로 복원되었음을 인정했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ restored just the way it was meant to be: 원문 그대로 ❌ ① built using only Western techniques: 동서양 기술 모두 사용 ❌ ② designed without any historical records: 기록이 있었음 ❌ ④ completely rebuilt from scratch: 복원이지 완전 재건이 아님
det.tip: authentic(진짜의) → 원래대로 복원되었음을 확인한 것이 핵심.

ch: restored just the way it was meant to be

questions.passage: He wanted it to be a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade as he hoped to make it the new capital, away from all the political chaos in Hanyang. So King Jeongjo gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them bring together the finest architectural techniques of his time from both the East and the West to build Hwaseong Fortress. __________
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 정조가 화성을 새 수도로 삼고자 한 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정조는 한양의 정치적 혼란에서 벗어나기 위해 화성을 새 수도로 만들고자 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① To escape the political instability in Hanyang: 원문 'away from all the political chaos in Hanyang' ❌ ② To be closer to China for trade: 본문에 없음 ❌ ③ To build a city near the ocean: 본문에 없음 ❌ ④ To honor his mother's birthplace: 본문에 없음
det.tip: chaos = 혼란, 무질서. political chaos in Hanyang = 한양의 정치적 혼란.

ch: To escape the political instability in Hanyang
To be closer to China for trade
To build a city near the ocean

questions.passage: So King Jeongjo gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them ①<u>bring</u> together the finest architectural techniques of his time from both the East and the West ②<u>to build</u> Hwaseong Fortress. He treated his people well during the construction of the fortress. They received fair wages and breaks during bad weather and ③<u>was</u> even paid when they were sick, something ④<u>that</u> was unheard of at that time.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: 그들은 공정한 임금과 악천후 시 휴식을 받았고, 아플 때도 급여를 ③받았다(were paid). 주어 They(복수)이므로 was → were.
det.analysis: ✅ ①②④ 어법 적절 ❌ ③ was → were: 주어 They(복수)에 맞춰야 함
det.tip: let + 목적어 + 동사원형(bring). to build = 목적 부사적 용법. that = 주격관계대명사.

questions.passage: This was not just about putting on a show. No, it was serious business. (A) [Lasted / Lasting] four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession moved alongside the king and his mother as they made a round trip to Hwaseong Haenggung. The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was (B) [to show / showing] respect to his family. It happened around his mother's sixtieth birthday. And his father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung. He was planning to hold a memorial service to honor his (C) [late / lately] father.
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 4일간 68km에 걸쳐 (A)지속되면서(Lasting): 분사구문. 정조가 마음에 품은 첫 번째 일은 가족에 대한 존경을 (B)보이는 것(to show): to부정사 보어. 돌아가신 (C)아버지(late father): late = 고(故).
det.analysis: ✅ ② (A) Lasting — (B) to show — (C) late: 분사구문+to부정사보어+형용사 ❌ ① Lasted는 분사구문에서 과거형 불가 ❌ ③ lately는 '최근에'라는 부사 ❌ ④ showing도 가능하나 was + to show가 더 자연스러움
det.tip: Lasting(지속하면서) = 분사구문. late father = 돌아가신 아버지 (lately ≠ late).

questions.passage: He treated his people well during the construction of the fortress. They received fair wages and breaks during bad weather and were even paid when they were sick, something that was unheard of at that time. Back then, ordinary people were typically required to work on public projects without getting paid. Once people got wind of King Jeongjo's plan, workers from all over the country came together in a rush. So, in under three years was the project finished, though it was initially thought to take about 10 years.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 정조는 노동자에게 공정한 임금, 악천후 휴식, 병가 급여를 제공했다. 전국에서 노동자가 몰려왔고 3년 만에 완공(원래 10년 예상).
det.analysis: ❌ ① Workers received pay even when they were sick: 원문 일치 ❌ ② Workers came from all over the country: 원문 일치 ❌ ③ The project was initially expected to take about 10 years: 원문 일치 ✅ ④ Only workers from Hanyang were allowed to participate: 전국에서 왔으므로 불일치
det.tip: all over the country = 전국에서. Hanyang만이 아님.

ch: Workers received pay even when they were sick.
Workers came from all over the country.
The project was initially expected to take about 10 years.
Only workers from Hanyang were allowed to participate.

questions.passage: Through the procession, King Jeongjo made government more accessible. During that time, the government used to hold exams to hire officials every three years. So, there weren't many chances available. He added special exams during the procession, giving more people a shot at joining the government. This move was innovative back then and made the government more diverse.
questions.stem: 정조가 행렬 중 시행한 특별 시험에 대해 옳은 설명은?

det.korean: 당시 관리 채용 시험은 3년마다 열렸으므로 기회가 적었다. 정조는 행렬 중 특별 시험을 추가하여 더 많은 사람에게 정부 참여 기회를 부여했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② It gave more people an opportunity to join the government: 원문 'giving more people a shot at joining the government' ❌ ① It replaced the regular exams entirely: 대체가 아닌 추가 ❌ ③ It was only open to military officials: 일반인도 참여 가능 ❌ ④ It was held every three years like regular exams: 행렬 중 특별히 열림
det.tip: added(추가했다) ≠ replaced(대체했다). 기존 시험에 더해 특별 시험을 열었다.

ch: It replaced the regular exams entirely.
It gave more people an opportunity to join the government.
It was only open to military officials.
It was held every three years like regular exams.

questions.passage: And among the records of the procession, there are these amazing paintings. One painting, Hwaneo Haengryeoldo, doesn't just ①<u>feature</u> the king's crew, but it also shows ordinary people watching along the road. It's a different ②<u>take</u> from the usual art of that time, which only ③<u>focused</u> on important figures. King Jeongjo's 1795 procession and Hwaseong Fortress stand as ④<u>denial</u> of that spirit.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정조의 1795년 행차와 화성은 그 정신의 ④증거(proof)로 남아 있다. denial(부정)은 proof(증거)의 반의어.
det.analysis: ✅ ①②③ 적절 ❌ ④ denial(부정) → proof(증거): '그 정신을 부정한다'가 아니라 '증명한다'
det.tip: proof(증거) ↔ denial(부정). stand as proof = ~의 증거로 남다.

questions.passage: In King Jeongjo's mind were big plans for Hwaseong. He wanted it to be a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade as he hoped to make it the new capital, away from all the political chaos in Hanyang. So King Jeongjo gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them bring together the finest architectural techniques of his time from both the East and the West to build Hwaseong Fortress. __________
questions.stem: 위 글로 보아, 정조가 화성 건설에 동서양의 건축 기술을 모두 활용한 근본적인 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 화성을 새 수도로 삼으려 했으므로, 최고 수준의 자급자족 도시를 만들기 위해 동서양의 최고 기술을 활용한 것.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ To build the best possible fortress for his envisioned new capital: 새 수도를 위한 최고의 요새 ❌ ① To impress foreign visitors with Western architecture: 외국 방문객 언급 없음 ❌ ② To compete with Chinese architectural achievements: 중국과 경쟁 언급 없음 ❌ ④ To create a monument for future tourists: 관광 목적 언급 없음
det.tip: self-sufficient city + new capital = 최고의 요새를 만들려는 근본적 이유.

ch: To impress foreign visitors with Western architecture
To compete with Chinese architectural achievements
To build the best possible fortress for his envisioned new capital
To create a monument for future tourists

questions.passage: ( ① ) He made sure everything was documented properly by creating records for the procession and the construction of Hwaseong Fortress. ( ② ) These construction records were especially a lifesaver when the fortress was damaged during wartime. ( ③ ) They were even part of why UNESCO recognized Hwaseong Fortress as a World Heritage Site. questions.stem:
다음 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은?

"And guess what? King Jeongjo didn't forget a single detail."

det.korean: '정조는 세부 사항 하나도 잊지 않았다'라는 문장은 기록을 만들었다는 내용 바로 앞에 와야 자연스럽다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① 문장 → '모든 것을 제대로 기록했다'로 이어짐 ❌ ② '기록이 구세주였다' 사이에 끼면 흐름 단절 ❌ ③ 유네스코 인정 앞에 끼면 맥락 불일치 ❌ ④ 유네스코의 불확실성 뒤에 오면 논리 단절
det.tip: 문장삽입 — 삽입 문장의 키워드('forget a single detail')가 다음 문장('documented properly')과 연결되는지 확인.

questions.passage:
다음 문장에서 원문과 다른 부분을 찾으시오.

"More than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and lots of important officials, all marching alongside the king and his ①father with 50 musicians playing ②traditional instruments. When they crossed a bridge made of ③36 boats on the Hangang River, you can imagine how that ④turned heads!"
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 원문과 다른 것은?

det.korean: 원문에서는 왕과 어머니(his mother)와 함께 행진했다. ① father → mother.
det.analysis: ✅ ② traditional: 원문 일치 ✅ ③ 36: 원문 일치 ✅ ④ turned heads: 원문 일치 ❌ ① father → mother: 원문은 'his mother'
det.tip: 오류찾기 — 원문의 세부 사항(인물, 숫자, 장소 등)을 정확히 기억하세요.

questions.passage:
[주어진 글] King Jeongjo's 1795 procession served multiple purposes beyond a simple royal journey.

(A) He added special exams during the procession, giving more people a shot at joining the government. This move was innovative back then and made the government more diverse.

(B) The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was to show respect to his family. It happened around his mother's sixtieth birthday, and his father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung.
